newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB sees little impact from new U.S. Zyrtec okay.
newsitem.headline: UCB sees little impact from new U.S. Zyrtec okay.

text.p: Belgian drugs and chemicals group UCB said on Thursday it expected recent U.S. approval of use of its Zyrtec anti-allergy drug on paediatric patients to have only a small impact on sales in the U.S.

"There will be a limited impact of sales in the U.S.," a UCB spokesman said after the company announced the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) gave the drug marketing clearance for child patients between the ages of six and 12.
He declined to give estimates of the impacts.
UCB said Zyrtec was the only one of recent anti-allergics to have gained the clearance.
Zyrtec now has FDA approval for three indications - seasonal allergies caused by pollen, year-round allergies caused by allergens such as dust mites and moulds, and hives and itching.
Sales of Zyrtec in the U.S., where since the start of 1996 the drug has been promoted jointly by UCB Pharma Inc and its licensee for the U.S., Pfizer Inc, stood at $82 million at the end of August.

The UCB spokesman said the company was sticking to its forecast of Zyrtec sales of $100 to $120 million in the U.S. this year, its first year of sales there. He noted that due to seasonal factors sales in the second half usually slowed down.
The market for anti-allergics for all age groups in the U.S. is estimated at $1.0 billion.
Current market leader is Schering Plough's Claritine.
